title: Truth and beauty (CCC 2500–2503)
hookLine: beauty expresses truth; art can raise the soul

lines: THE END OF THE SECTION ON TRUTH.
ARTISTS, AND ART MADE FOR CHURCHES.
cards: The Catechism's section on the eighth commandment covers lying, false witness, gossip, oaths and the media. Then, in its closing paragraphs, it turns somewhere unexpected: beauty.
The work of artists, and the art made for churches. A commandment about not lying ends with a word about art. Why put truth and beauty in the same room?

teach.b: The Catechism's claim is simple: truth is beautiful in itself. Words are one way truth gets told, but not the only one.
Truth can find other forms of expression, above all when what has to be said is beyond words: the depths of the heart, the mystery of God.

teach.h: THE MAKER SEEN IN WHAT HE MADE.
teach.b: It draws this from the Book of Wisdom: from the greatness and beauty of created things, their maker can be seen, by comparison. Behind every sunset, in that reading, is an artist.

Then it turns to human art: a form of practical wisdom, a gift of the Creator, joining knowledge and skill to give form to the truth of something. A carpenter, a singer and a painter are all doing it.
Art resembles God's own work of making, so far as it's inspired by truth and love of creatures.

Sacred art, it says, is true and beautiful when its form matches its purpose: to call to mind and glorify, in faith and adoration, the mystery of God. Art like that can draw a person toward prayer, toward the love of God.
And bishops get a job: to promote sacred art, and to keep out of churches anything that doesn't serve that purpose. So a church window isn't decoration added after the teaching.
In Catholic thinking, it's a way of telling the truth. The week, in brief: every life; care, not worship; whole, not divided; goods are for all; entrusted; guard reputations; and now this.

how: In Catholic churches, painting, sculpture, stained glass, music and architecture are meant to point to God, and the Church asks bishops to promote sacred art that serves worship.

games.q: the Catechism's section on the eighth commandment, about truth, comes to its closing paragraphs. what does it turn to?
games.why: it turns to beauty: truth is beautiful in itself, and art, especially sacred art, can tell the truth and draw people toward God.

practice: Choose one beautiful thing within reach, a painting on your phone, a photo of a church window, a bowl on the shelf, the light on the wall right now.

Don't analyze it; look slowly, the way you'd listen to someone you love, noticing color, then shape, then what it seems to say without words. If you pray, let the looking become thanks; if you don't, just stay with it a while.

wordCard.voice: Truth and beauty. In Catholic teaching, truth is beautiful in itself, and real beauty, in creation and in art, can tell the truth and lift a person toward God. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: beauty is true. Some truths are told best without any words. That's the week.
